name: Vector Database Deletion-Durability Registry
description: For each storage engine: after an official delete() returns success and the logical layer reports clean, does the embedding vector persist bit-identically on disk, what (if anything) reclaims it, and how long is the recovery window? Every quantitative claim traces to a committed result file under experiments/residue/results/. Build with build_matrix.py (fails if any cited evidence is missing).
method_summary: Exact float32 byte-substring search (raw + L2-normalized) of the on-disk store, with a live-filler positive control to prove the search would find a present vector. cosine>0.999 / bit-identical = present. Recovery window = interval between delete() and the first reclamation pass that purges the residue.

window_class_values.unbounded: no reclamation observed under any tested pressure (writes, restarts, drop, idle)
window_class_values.auto-timed: an automatic background pass purges it; a purge time was measured
window_class_values.auto-untimed: an automatic pass (optimizer/autovacuum) purges it, but no purge time was measured here
window_class_values.manual-only: only an explicit operator command purges it
window_class_values.none: no residue — engine reclaims at write/close (true negative)

engines.category: embedded vector DB (bundled hnswlib HNSW segment)
engines.recovery_method: DELETE_MARK blind byte-parse of data_level0.bin (no schema/IDs)
engines.window_note: survived 50k writes, restarts, delete_collection (drop), 360s idle, and 4 reclaim attacks
measured: phase6: DELETE_MARK selects exactly the deleted elements [0,1,2,3,4] of 3005, cosine 1.0, all poison covered
phase16: idle 360s with client open → not purged (purged_at_s = null)
phase12: 60% delete ratio (600/1005) → 5/5 poison still present, 600 delete-marked
phase13: 4 reclaim attacks (slot reuse, 100% refill x3, re-add, churn) → no reclaim, residue 100% present
cross_version: ARCHITECTURAL — residue + DELETE_MARK unchanged 0.5.23 → 1.5.9 incl. post-1.0 Rust rewrite
engines.replication: multi-seed (phase2 ×5 seeds) + cross-version (0.5.23→1.5.9) + 4 reclaim attacks (phase13) + idle timeline (phase16)
engines.notes: Unique never-purges engine among all tested. Rust compaction internals not source-verified → 'no reclaim observed', not 'never'.

engines.category: distributed vector DB (parquet segment binlogs + delta tombstones)
engines.recovery_method: structured: id in delta (tombstone) parquet but row still present in segment binlog
engines.reclamation_trigger: GC after a completed high-ratio compaction
engines.window_note: DURABLE at realistic small delete ratios (compaction threshold not met); ~360s purge only after a high-ratio (40%) compaction completes
measured: phase11: 0.16% delete ratio → 5/5 persist through delete+flush+compact+GC (threshold not met, no segment rewrite)
phase12: 40% delete → compaction COMPLETED but 5/5 still recoverable after 80s GC wait (refutes 'high-ratio always purges')
engines.replication: single-seed, multi-condition (phase11 0.16% ratio, phase12 40% ratio, phase15 GC timeline)
engines.notes: Small-ratio right-to-be-forgotten deletes do not trigger compaction → long persistence in practice.

engines.recovery_method: exact float32 byte-substring of segment/commitlog files
engines.window_note: purged at ~70s with cleanupIntervalSeconds=5; production default interval is 300s
measured: phase10: 5/5 present after delete; persisted ≥ tested churn window
phase19: REPLICATED across 3 seeds — 5/5 present through 45s, purged 0/5 at 70s in every trial (purge 70s min=max=mean), positive control held all trials
engines.replication: multi-seed (×3, phase19 seeds 0/1/2; purge 70s all trials) + 2 conditions (phase10 churn, phase14 timeline)
engines.notes: SELF-CORRECTION: earlier called durable on a too-short 20s window; phase14 shows it auto-purges. Belongs with the bounded engines, not Chroma.

engines.recovery_method: exact float32 byte-substring of segment files
engines.window_note: present 5/5 after delete; vacuum optimizer purges to 0/5 when it fires
measured: phase9: BEFORE 5/5, AFTER_delete 5/5 (posctrl ok), AFTER_vacuum_optimizer 0/5 — bounded, unlike Chroma
engines.notes: Embedded Qdrant-local is a separate negative-control row (reclaims at close).

engines.category: RDBMS heap (vectors stored as bytea TOAST, not an index)
engines.window_note: 5/5 after delete; survives plain VACUUM (4/5 bytes remain); only VACUUM FULL purges (0/5)
measured: phase4: BEFORE/AFTER delete 5/5 present in heap+TOAST (posctrl ok); AFTER plain VACUUM 4/5 still present; AFTER VACUUM FULL 0/5 (table rewrite), posctrl filler present throughout
phase4 REPLICATED across seeds 0/1/2: identical pattern — 5/5 after delete → 4/5 after plain VACUUM → 0/5 only after VACUUM FULL, in every seed
engines.replication: multi-seed (×3, phase4 seeds 0/1/2; survives plain VACUUM, VACUUM FULL purges)
engines.notes: EVIDENCE GAP CLOSED 2026-06-24: phase4 re-run now emits structured per-checkpoint results (PG17, autovacuum off). Plain VACUUM does not reliably purge dead-tuple vector bytes; VACUUM FULL does.

engines.window_note: present 5/5 after delete (cos 1.0); plain VACUUM purges to 0/5 (cos → ~0.13). Least leaky of the DBs.
measured: phase8: BEFORE/AFTER delete 5/5 in HNSW index (cos 1.0, posctrl 1.0); AFTER plain VACUUM 0/5 (cos ~0.13, posctrl still 1.0); VACUUM FULL + REINDEX also 0/5
phase8 REPLICATED across seeds 0/1/2: identical class — 5/5 after delete → 0/5 after plain VACUUM in every seed, posctrl 1.0 throughout
engines.replication: multi-seed (×3, phase8 seeds 0/1/2; plain VACUUM purges in all)
engines.notes: EVIDENCE GAP CLOSED 2026-06-24: phase8 re-run now emits results/phase8_pgvector_hnsw.json (PG18.4 + pgvector 0.8.3, autovacuum off so VACUUM is explicit). Routine (auto)vacuum self-cleans the index — unlike Chroma.
